title: Transient RBAC grant leakage during KMS rollover causing missing audit traces
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported missing or incomplete audit log entries and unexpected temporary RBAC elevations during KMS envelope key rollover on Private clusters. The issue appears when control-plane rewrap jobs overlap with rolebinding refreshes, resulting in transient grant entries that are not reconciled in the audit stream and occasionally allow short-lived elevated token bindings. This ticket drives an urgent patch, rollout plan, and stakeholder comms.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-08 02:14 UTC: First support alert (CS-2109) from Acme Health - missing audit events correlated with scheduled KMS rewrap
2026-03-09 18:37 UTC: Support triage noted similar reports from two Dedicated customers; escalated to infra-oncall
2026-03-10 00:22 UTC: Engineering reproduction confirmed: rolebinding refresh + async rewrap race leads to orphaned grant record causing audit omission
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC: Customer calls with security teams; raised priority to P0 and created ENG-754321
2026-03-12 21:54 UTC: Initial mitigation applied (throttle rewrap concurrency) for affected clusters; partial restoration of audit continuity observed
2026-03-14 07:15 UTC: Patch candidate branched and integration tests added; rolling canary scheduled
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a Private control plane with KMS envelope rewrap scheduled (short interval for test).
2) Trigger a rolebinding resync (e.g., via tenant-role-propagation job) concurrent with rewrap window.
3) Observe authz service logs: a grant creation event written locally but removed by the rewrap cleanup path before audit forwarder de-duplicates.
4) Check audit pipeline: missing grant events, followed by a reconciliation event that is suppressed due to dedupe TTL, causing permanent audit gap for that operation.
technical_analysis: Root cause: race between async KMS rewrap garbage-collection (unwrap+rewrap cleanup) and the rolebinding reconciliation pipeline. When rewrap removes intermediate key metadata, the audit forwarding path writes a grant record referencing a key alias that is later mutated; forwarder dedupe logic drops the follow-up reconciliation event because it appears duplicate under the old alias TTL window.

Secondary issue: token binding code allowed optimistic promotion of ephemeral service tokens during the narrow window between grant creation and metadata re-attach, which in edge cases resulted in elevated requests accepted for <2s.
Area ownership: AuthZ service (team: identity), KMS rewrap controller (team: infra-kms), and Audit forwarder (team: observability).
immediate_mitigation: Applied action: reduced concurrent rewrap workers to 1 on affected clusters (2026-03-12), preventing new race windows.
Config change: enabled strict audit-forwarder dedupe logging to capture suppressed reconciliation events (flag: AUDIT_DEDUPE_DEBUG=true).
Customer guidance: notified impacted customers that transient elevation window was short (<2s) and we are pushing a hard patch; recommended they rotate long-lived service credentials if concerned.
patch_plan: Fix: make rewrap controller perform 'reconcile-and-freeze' handshake with rolebinding reconciler: rewrap will now emit a pre-commit token that blocks rolebinding promotion until rewrap finalization completes.
Fix: update audit-forwarder dedupe algorithm to consider alias lineage (map old alias -> new alias) during TTL window so reconciliation events are not discarded.
Safety: add a short-lived guard in token binder that rejects optimistic promotions when metadata mutation is in-progress.
Testing: unit tests for alias lineage mapping, e2e test simulating concurrent rewrap+rolebinding flows, and a chaos test with accelerated rewrap windows.
rollout_and_qa: Canary: deploy to two non-prod private clusters and one low-traffic customer-private cluster (scheduled 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC).
Monitoring: add alert rule for any authz elevation >500ms in canary clusters and pipeline-level metric for audit-forwarder suppressed_event_count delta.
Rollback plan: if suppressed_event_count increases or canary customers report missing events, revert to concurrency-throttle and roll forward a follow-up patch.

next_steps: Finish code changes and get approvals from identity and infra-kms codeowners (requested reviews).
Merge PRs and run canary deployment 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC; monitor for 6 hours then expand if stable.
Complete security review and add follow-up ticket for audit retention backfill for affected time ranges.
Publish customer-facing incident report and remediation guidance after canary success.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add lineage-aware dedupe to audit-forwarder (owner: observability).
2) Instrument rewrap controller to emit 'in-progress' annotations that downstream services can observe (owner: infra-kms).
3) Harden token binding to reject optimistic promotions if any dependent metadata mutation is active (owner: identity).
4) Create automated backfill job to replay suppressed reconciliation events for last 72 hours (owner: observability).
